newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state cancels 100,000T Brazil sugar deal.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state cancels 100,000T Brazil sugar deal.

text.p: The Egyptian government has scrapped a contract to buy 100,000 tonnes of Brazilian refined sugar which was to be delivered in June, an official at the supply ministry said on Wednesday.
The official said Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily cancelled the deal to protect the local state-owned refineries which sell traders refined sugar at higher prices.

"We bought the sugar, the best quality, for about 1,300 pounds ($382.9) a tonne and we get lesser quality sugar from the state companies for 1,500 pounds per tonne. It was a good deal but the state was worried about the competition," he added.

Egypt imports about 300,000 tonnes of raw sugar a year which is refined by local firms, most of them state-owned. The biggest is the Sugar and Integrated Industries Company (SIIC) which the government has said it would partly privatise soon.
